message.content:
**Hydrogen (H)** – the simplest and most abundant element in the universe – has a rich set of physical, chemical, and nuclear properties that make it unique among the elements. Below is a comprehensive overview of its key characteristics: | Property | Value / Description | |----------|---------------------| | **Atomic number** | 1 | | **Symbol** | H | | **Standard atomic weight** | 1.008 u (average of isotopes) | | **Isotopes** |
  • ¹H (protium) – 99.98 % natural abundance, one proton, no neutrons.
  • ²H (deuterium) – 0.02 % natural abundance, one proton + one neutron.
  • ³H (tritium) – radioactive, half‑life ≈12.32 yr, one proton + two neutrons.
| | **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ | | **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 | | **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) | | **Electron affinity** | –72.8 kJ mol⁻¹ (negative because energy is released when an electron is added) | | **Boiling point (STP)** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) | | **Melting point (STP)** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) | | **Density (at STP)** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ (≈0.0000899 kg m⁻³) | | **Molar volume (ideal gas, 273 K, 1 atm)** | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ | | **Specific heat capacity (gas, 25 °C)** | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ | | **Thermal conductivity (gas, 25 °C)** | 0.1805 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ | | **Electrical conductivity (metallic hydrogen, high pressure)** | ~10⁶ S m⁻¹ (under extreme pressures >400 GPa) | | **Reactivity** | Extremely reactive; forms hydrides with metals, acids, and many nonmetals. Combines with oxygen to form water (exothermic). | | **Bonding behavior** | Forms covalent bonds (H₂), ionic bonds (as H⁺ or H⁻), and participates in hydrogen bonding (in water, alcohols, etc.). | | **Spectral lines** | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible), Paschen series (IR); characteristic emission/absorption lines used in astrophysics. | | **Nuclear spin** | Protium (I=½), Deuterium (I=1), Tritium (I=½). | | **Magnetic moment** | 2.7928473446 µ_N (proton magnetic moment). | | **Phase diagram** | Under normal pressure, exists as a diatomic gas; under very high pressure (>400 GPa) predicted to become metallic and possibly superconducting. | ### Key Physical & Chemical Highlights 1. **Lightest Element** - Lowest molar mass (1.00794 g mol⁻¹). - Extremely low density makes it useful as a lifting gas (balloons, airships). 2. **Highly Reactive** - Strong oxidizer; reacts violently with halogens, fluorine, and many metals. - Combustion produces water vapor: `2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O` (ΔH° = –483.6 kJ mol⁻¹). 3. **Unique Bonding** - Forms a single covalent bond in H₂ (σ bond). - In water, each H atom participates in two hydrogen bonds, giving water its high surface tension and specific heat. 4. **Astrophysical Importance** - Dominant component of stars (hydrogen fusion powers the Sun). - Spectral lines (Balmer, Lyman) are diagnostic tools for stellar composition and temperature. 5. **Isotope Effects** - Deuterium and tritium have distinct nuclear properties; deuterium is used in heavy water reactors, tritium in nuclear weapons and fusion research. 6. **High‑Pressure Behavior** - At >400 GPa, theoretical predictions suggest a transition to a metallic state with potential room‑temperature superconductivity. 7. **Safety Considerations** - Extremely flammable; requires careful handling to avoid explosions. - Trichloride of hydrogen (HCl) is corrosive; tritium is radioactive and requires containment. --- #### Quick Reference Table (Standard Conditions) | Property | Value | |----------|-------| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C | | Melting point | –259.16 °C | | Density | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ | | Ionization energy | 13.598 eV | | Electron affinity | –72.8 kJ mol⁻¹ | | Electronegativity | 2.20 | | Molar volume | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ | These properties collectively define hydrogen’s role across chemistry, physics, engineering, and astronomy.
